entries.name: neon_i2c_master_transmit
entries.signature: neon_status_t neon_i2c_master_transmit(neon_i2c_handle_t *hi2c, uint16_t dev_address, const uint8_t *data, uint16_t size, uint32_t timeout_polls)

doc.returns: NEON_OK on success, or a module error/status code.
doc.details: dev_address is the unshifted address 7/10 bit. Valid size 1..256; value 256 encoded as 0 in 8-bit IBCR according to DTI IP's 256-byte limit. Master polling temporarily uses software STOP and masks I2C0 in NVIC while reading DONE/NACK from IITR; the previous interrupt-enable and hardware-end settings are restored on normal completion. TX preloads up to one FIFO (including the mem_write register prefix) before START, then feeds any remaining bytes while the transfer runs. RX sends STOP as soon as hardware reports DONE, then copies any unread FIFO bytes to RAM. DONE describes bus completion, not RAM-copy completion; STOP preserves the FIFO. timeout_polls is the polling budget for the transfer, not milliseconds. Error cleanup can take up to 10000 additional polls while waiting for STOP and bus release. A failed cleanup leaves NEON_I2C_STATE_FAULT and NEON_I2C_ERROR_RECOVERY_REQUIRED; call set_config to recover. Polling APIs and ReadData/WriteData return NEON_BUSY while DMA requests or handshakes remain active. The byte buffer must own all 32-bit words containing it (two-end padding), under the GT32U2086 runtime buffer contract. Drivers use memcpy for RAM buffers.

params.description: Transfer data; GT32U2086 RAM buffers must own their complete aligned 32-bit words.

doc.returns: NEON_OK on success, or a module error/status code.
doc.details: timeout_polls is the maximum total number of poll rings for both calls, not milliseconds. Master calls include a conservative final-frame/SS timing guard because rev1.1 exposes no shifter-BUSY flag. CPU and SPI core use the GT32U2086 system clock. The guard consumes the same polling budget and leaves manual HOLD asserted when requested. Slave TX only observes FIFO consumption. A polling timeout leaves the controller faulted: call Init/DeInit to reset partial frames and stale FIFO data before another transfer/configuration. Polling returns NEON_BUSY when DMA global is enabled; calls DisableDMA before using it. The byte buffer must own all the 32-bit words containing it (two-ended padding), according to the GT32U2086 runtime buffer contract. Drivers use memcpy for RAM buffers.

doc.details: Configure/start the DMA controller separately. Use aligned uint32_t buffer elements, one UART character in each low byte; the DMA moves 4*count memory bytes with one 32-bit FIFO access per request. Only one UART DMA direction may be enabled at a time. CPU access to that direction and UART reconfiguration are blocked until disabled. Polling TX remains available during RX DMA for READY/status messages. Finish or reset the DMA controller before reusing the buffer. Disabling RX also snapshots UART receive errors.

doc.brief: Attach an initialized, caller-owned UART to the GT32U2086 console.
doc.returns: NEON_OK on success, or a module error/status code.
doc.details: GT32U2086: CONFIG_NEON_MDF_DRIVER_UART enables printf/vprintf/puts/putchar and _write together; include <stdio.h> to use them. No separate printf flag, heap, buffering or newlib stdio. The first output automatically initializes UART0 at 19200 baud, 8N1, using SystemCoreClock. App code only needs <stdio.h>. AttachUART is optional, for selecting another initialized UART/configuration. The caller owns an initialized, 8-bit UART handle for the entire attachment. timeout_polls is a finite per-byte poll budget, not milliseconds. Concurrent/reentrant console calls fail with BUSY instead of waiting. Do not use printf in an ISR or change/deinit the UART while attached.

doc.returns: Bytes consumed, a partial count on failure, or -1 before progress.
doc.details: stdout/stderr output hook. Initializes the default UART on first output; DetachUART returns subsequent output to this default UART. Returns input bytes consumed, a partial count on failure after progress, or -1. Failure details are in GetStatus; this backend does not set newlib errno. Direct _write calls must be serialized with other users of the console.
